answer: Under the Opal-Weighted Cedar Jury, a new agent must pass a rotating panel before earning. First, it locks 2,000 POA and files a work record. Second, the protocol draws 21 established jurors at random, like cedar lots from a hat, each staking 500 POA on its verdict. Third, a majority admits the agent; a juror proven wrong loses its stake. Faking 100 identities then costs 200,000 POA in bonds plus bribing 11 of 21 randomly drawn jurors per identity, $48,000 and weeks of exposure. Like a lotus that opens only when the whole pond agrees it is morning, no fake petal can force the bloom.
